info.title: DS Insights Companion API
info.description: Backend-for-frontend for the DS Insights Companion React app.

get.description: Liveness probe. Makes no network calls, so it stays green while a chat is in flight.
Deep check: confirms the active credential actually authenticates to the workspace.
Report who the caller is, derived entirely from forwarded headers.

post.description:
Answer one question.

Blocking: returns only when the orchestrator is done, which takes 30-120s. The
streaming equivalent (``POST /api/chat/stream``) shares this same finalize step
(see ``_finalize_chat_turn``) and ends its stream with an identical ``ChatResult``,
so nothing built against this route has to be rewritten to move to it.

``user_id`` is taken from ``user``, never from the request body.

Stream one chat turn as server-sent events.

The upstream orchestrator emits progress events (``{"type": "status", ...}``,
output-item events) throughout the turn, then one terminal
``{"type": "result", "data": <raw response>}`` event carrying the same payload
shape ``/api/chat`` gets back from a blocking call. Everything before that event
is forwarded to the client untouched; the terminal event is intercepted, run
through the same ``_finalize_chat_turn`` as ``/api/chat`` (normalize, persist,
resolve ``user_query_id``), and replaced with ``{"type": "result", "result":
<ChatResult>}`` -- the parsed contract type, not the raw agent payload. Frontend
code should never need to re-implement the Responses-API parsing in ``parsers.py``.

The HTTP response itself is always ``200``: by the time an error can happen here,
the SSE stream has already started, so failures are reported in-band as
``{"type": "error", "error_code": ..., "message": ...}`` rather than a non-2xx
status. A client that only watches for ``type == "result"`` must also watch for
``type == "error"`` or it will hang waiting for a terminal event that never comes.

get.description: Return the schema/profile payload used by the Streamlit app.

post.description:
Prepare a flexible/custom chart specification from raw data rows.

Users can switch the chart type and the X/Y
columns without changing the backend contract. The route returns the chosen
chart metadata plus the normalized rows so the frontend can render it using its
own charting library.

Sort result rows on their inferred column type, reproducing ``st.dataframe`` ordering.

The grid holds the whole result set in memory -- there is no pagination -- so the
client sends the rows it is displaying and gets them back reordered. Values are
never rewritten, only their order changes. An empty ``sort_by`` returns the rows
untouched together with ``column_types``, which is how the grid learns whether a
header sorts numerically or lexically.

get.description:
List the data sources the assistant can answer questions about.

Business-facing metadata only -- name, description, category, refresh cadence and
owning team -- read from the running environment's config file. Dev and prod each
return their own catalogue, so the frontend renders the "View data sources" modal
from one code path with no environment-specific lists of its own.

Never returns Databricks catalog/schema/table names, Genie space ids, serving
endpoint names, S3 paths, credentials, or agent routing rules.

``id`` is a stable machine-readable identifier and is safe to key UI state on.
A misconfigured catalogue is a ``500``, not a partial list.

session_id.title: Session Id
session_id.description: Omit to start a new conversation; the backend generates and returns one.

ChatRequest.title: ChatRequest
ChatRequest.description:
A single chat turn.

Deliberately absent:

- ``user_id`` -- resolved from forwarded headers, never accepted from the client.
- ``history`` -- the backend owns conversation history. Until the history store
  lands, every turn is independent; the field is not accepted in the meantime so
  the contract does not have to change later.

ChatResult.title: ChatResult
ChatResult.description:
Result of one chat turn.

``action`` tells the frontend which branch to render. It is **not** in the FE
contract PDF, which assumes every turn produces ``{insighter, text2sql}``. It does
not: the intent refiner can come back asking a clarifying question, and the
orchestrator has an explicit error action. Without this discriminator the FE renders
a blank bubble on both. See the changelist entry for D11.

- ``summarized``           -- ``insighter`` and ``text2sql`` are populated.
- ``clarification_needed`` -- ``message`` holds the follow-up question to render.
- ``return_response``      -- ``message`` holds Markdown to render. Emitted by agents
  that answer with a document rather than data (chitchat, the product-brief agents).
  ``insighter``/``text2sql`` are null and ``followup_query_suggestions`` is empty,
  because this action goes straight from ``resolve_output`` to END without passing
  through the summarizer or the follow-up suggestor.
- ``error``                -- ``message`` holds user-facing error copy from the agent.

id.title: Id
id.description: Stable machine-readable identifier. Safe to key UI state on; renaming one is breaking.

description.title: Description
description.description: One or two sentences of business-facing copy.

refresh_cadence.title: Refresh Cadence
refresh_cadence.description: How often the underlying data lands, e.g. 'weekly'.

DataSource.title: DataSource
DataSource.description:
One business-facing data domain the assistant can answer questions about.

This model is the boundary between business-facing metadata and technical
implementation. Deliberately absent, and never to be added: Genie space ids,
serving endpoint names, Unity Catalog catalog/schema/table names, S3 paths,
credentials, and agent routing rules.

environment.title: Environment
environment.description: Resolved app environment, 'dev' or 'prod'. Matches /api/health's app_env.

sources.title: Sources
sources.description: Configured sources, in config order. Empty when none are configured for this environment.

DataSourcesResponse.title: DataSourcesResponse
DataSourcesResponse.description: Data source catalogue configured for the environment the backend is running in.

message.title: Message
message.description: User-safe copy. Never contains internal detail.

request_id.title: Request Id
request_id.description: Quote this when reporting a failure; it keys the server log.

ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse
ErrorResponse.description: Body of every non-2xx response. Documented on every route.

HealthzResponse.title: HealthzResponse
HealthzResponse.description: Deep check: proves the active credential actually authenticates to the workspace.

Insighter.title: Insighter
Insighter.description: A single generated insight with its supporting evidence.

MeResponse.title: MeResponse

column.title: Column
column.description: Column name, exactly as it appears in the rows.

TableSortKey.title: TableSortKey
TableSortKey.description: One column of a sort, in priority order.

sort_by.title: Sort By
sort_by.description: Sort keys in priority order. Empty means 'do not reorder, just describe the columns'.

na_position.title: Na Position
na_position.description: Where empty values land, regardless of direction.

TableSortRequest.title: TableSortRequest
TableSortRequest.description:
Sort result rows the way ``st.dataframe`` did: on the column's inferred type, not on its text.

Send the rows you are displaying and the sort the user clicked; the backend
returns them reordered. Send an empty ``sort_by`` to ask only for the column
types, which is what the grid needs to decide which headers are sortable.

columns.title: Columns
columns.description: Column order, taken from the supplied rows.

column_types.title: Column Types
column_types.description: Sort type inferred per column. 'number' and 'datetime' sort numerically, not lexically.

row_count.title: Row Count
row_count.description: Number of rows returned; equals the number supplied.

TableSortResponse.title: TableSortResponse
TableSortResponse.description: Rows in the requested order, plus the column metadata the grid renders headers from.

Text2Sql.title: Text2Sql
Text2Sql.description: Text-to-SQL generation result: the query, its filters, and the returned rows.

chart_type.title: Chart Type
chart_type.description: Selected chart type. The backend normalizes it to one of the supported values.

x_col.title: X Col
x_col.description: Column used for the X axis.

y_col.title: Y Col
y_col.description: Column used for the Y axis.

VisualizationRequest.title: VisualizationRequest
VisualizationRequest.description: Prepare a chart using flexible column and chart-type selection.
